overall_assessment: Reviewed all 28 fetched courses (20 suspects and 8 random controls) and all 5 failed-fetch entries: core plan sections, facts and academic-year selection are generally faithful, with no demonstrated wrong-page or wrong-year extraction. The 18 uncaptured suspects mostly reflect intentionally omitted year pickers and exam logistics, but six also lose substantive assessment-change comments; the two short suspects reflect sparse source pages, and the failed-fetch URLs do not establish that an available plan was missed. A template label contaminates all 28 extracts, while random controls expose source-inherited glued learning-outcome headings and malformed punctuation; credit-reduction tables retain readable tab-separated cells.

findings.evidence: 1) Merk at eksamensform er endret til hjemmeeksamen som et smittevernstiltak i den pågående koronasituasjonen.
findings.description: Six of the 28 fetched plans omit the exam-tab comments explaining temporary changes to assessment form: TS200114, the 2019-autumn FY8918, KLMED8004, MV2013 and NEVR3002 offerings, and 2022-spring BI2014. The changed exam forms and their numbered footnote references remain, but the explanations are absent; MV2013 therefore retains an oral-assessment description alongside a home-exam listing without the comment reconciling them. These are real uncaptured-content flags under the rubric and course_plan_spec.md, which explicitly retain COVID changes to assessment design; omitted dates, times, rooms and year pickers are not part of this finding.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/institution_config.R unconditionally excludes #omEksamen ul.portlet-msg-info in the NTNU configuration. The stored MV2013 HTML puts the substantive change notice in li.exam-comments inside precisely that excluded list.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the blanket #omEksamen ul.portlet-msg-info exclusion with filtering of individual logistics-only messages. Retain li.exam-comments messages containing assessment changes, including "eksamensform er endret" and "exam form has changed", with their numbered references; continue excluding exam dates and rooms.

findings.description: All 28 fetched extracts include the literal implementation label "course-details-portlet" between the page title and course code. This is recurring non-plan template text, including in every random control, and is missed by the junk pre-pass. The course title, code, facts box and staff information are not defects in this check.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The #content selector includes h2.portlet-title-text, whose literal text in the stored NTNU HTML is "course-details-portlet"; the NTNU exclude list does not remove that element.
findings.suggested_fix: Add #content h2.portlet-title-text to the NTNU exclude configuration, leaving the actual course title, course code and facts box intact.

findings.evidence: KunnskaperStudenten har- inngående kunnskap om pedagogiske, faglige og etiske styrker og svakheter ved ulike former for vurdering og kartlegging - inn
findings.description: One random control has its entire learning-outcome section in a single paragraph with glued headings and words: "KunnskaperStudenten har", "undervisningenFerdigheterStudenten kan" and "skoleGenerell kompetanseStudenten kan". The text remains present, but the knowledge, skills and competence structure is unreadable and fails the rubric's separation of headings and paragraphs. This local defect escapes the wall flag because the rest of the extract has normal line breaks.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The stored source HTML already contains these exact glued strings in a single p.content-learning-goal with no intervening markup or whitespace. This is inherited source formatting, not evidence that the DOM walker discarded existing paragraph breaks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a narrowly scoped NTNU text normalization for the observed glued heading sequences: insert paragraph breaks before Kunnskaper, Ferdigheter and Generell kompetanse when directly joined to Studenten, and insert a line break before the following Studenten har/kan phrase. Apply this only to these exact recognizable sequences rather than splitting arbitrary capitalized words.

findings.evidence: To be announced by each Lecturer, but typically it is Principles of Neural Science, Kandel, Schwartz and Jessel.
findings.description: Three fetched plans, including random control BK3380, retain C1 control characters in place of punctuation: U+0095 as learning-outcome bullets, U+0092 as an apostrophe, U+0093/U+0094 around a reading-list title, and U+0091 before common space. These produce malformed visible punctuation despite otherwise readable text; substantive prose is not missing.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The stored HTML already contains these C1 characters, consistent with Windows-1252 punctuation previously interpreted as Latin-1. R/extract_fulltext.R and the NTNU configuration pass the source characters through without normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the observed C1 punctuation in an NTNU post_fn: map U+0091/U+0092 to opening/closing single quotation marks, U+0093/U+0094 to opening/closing double quotation marks, and U+0095 to a bullet. Use explicit character substitution rather than recoding the entire UTF-8 document.
